long_biography.plain_text:
Fresh out of college in the early 1980s, Lewis Swezy studied the economics of a 16-unit Section 8 project his mother, Ruby Stripling Swezy, was developing. Raised by schoolteachers in blue-collar Hialeah, he was drawn to the stability of rent supported by federal housing programmes. The pair later used low-income housing tax credits before ending their business partnership in 2000.

Swezy subsequently operated as an independent developer, using land purchases, entitlements and resales to generate capital. Through Centennial Management, RS Development and RS Construction, he combined acquisition, financing, building and property management, concentrating on affordable multifamily communities in South Florida. The portfolio expanded into thousands of regulated apartments, market-rate housing, industrial space and development land. Public housing-finance records identify him as a principal and guarantor across multiple projects.
